claims.statement: FDA lists Melanotan II in the bulk drug substances nominated-but-withdrawn table on its 503A compounding safety-risk reference page, citing immunogenicity risk from aggregation/peptide-related impurities and noting published case reports of serious adverse events including melanoma, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome, sympathomimetic toxidrome, and priapism. No Melanotan II product is FDA-approved for any indication.

claims.statement: Melanotan II (PubChem CID 92432, molecular formula C50H69N15O9, MW ~1024.2 g/mol) is an unlicensed, largely untested peptide with no approved medical use; regulatory and clinical-reference sources describe it as not recommended for use outside of research/clinical-trial settings.

claims.statement: In a double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover human study of 20 men with psychogenic and organic erectile dysfunction, subcutaneous Melanotan II at 0.025 mg/kg produced penile erection in 17 of 20 men (mean 41 minutes of Rigiscan tip rigidity >80%) and increased reported sexual desire after 68% of active doses versus 19% of placebo doses (P<0.01); this is investigational sexual-function data, not evidence supporting tanning-oriented or cosmetic use, and Melanotan II remains unapproved for any indication.

context.useCase: investigational erectile dysfunction/sexual desire research (not an approved use)
context.doseText: 0.025 mg/kg, single-dose crossover protocol (trial protocol; not a use recommendation)

claims.statement: Short-term adverse effects documented with Melanotan II include facial flushing, reduced appetite/nausea/vomiting, and spontaneous erections (priapism) occurring 1-5 hours after administration; the human RCT literature separately documents nausea and yawning as frequent side effects, with severe nausea in 12.9% of subjects at the 0.025 mg/kg dose.

claims.statement: Longer-term and serious safety concerns reported with Melanotan II use include melanoma, deepening/changes of moles and new atypical melanocytic naevi, and rare severe vascular/systemic events; a published case report describes a 45-year-old man who developed right-sided renal infarction (approximately 50% of kidney affected) after self-administering 27 mg of Melanotan II subcutaneously over six months for tanning, with the authors proposing Melanotan II-induced vasoconstriction/thrombotic effect as the mechanism after excluding embolic and coagulation causes.

claims.statement: Melanotan II is widely marketed online and among gray-market peptide vendors as a 'tanning peptide' and libido enhancer for unsupervised, repeated self-injection, but no Melanotan II product is FDA-approved for tanning, cosmetic, or sexual-function use; the only controlled human efficacy data identified concerns single-dose, clinically supervised erectile-function outcomes, not chronic self-administered tanning, and it does not establish safety for long-term unsupervised use. Regulators and clinical references instead document a safety signal (melanoma, mole changes, priapism, vascular events, immunogenicity) associated with real-world gray-market use.

conflicts.summary: Online/vendor marketing of Melanotan II as a general tanning and libido peptide for repeated self-injection is not supported by the identified evidence, which consists of a single small supervised single-dose erectile-function trial and an unapproved regulatory status with an accumulating case-report safety signal (melanoma, renal infarction, priapism).

Primary PubMed/PMC pages for the rhabdomyolysis case report (Clinical Toxicology, PMID 23121206) and a second melanoma case report (PMID 24355990) could not be fetched this session (blocked by an interstitial/CAPTCHA); their claims are only indirectly corroborated via the FDA page's case-report summary and should be independently verified against the primary sources at review time.
FDA bulk drug substances page listings and table placement are subject to periodic revision; confirm Melanotan II's current table/category status against the live page at review time.

Human evidence base is thin: only one controlled human trial (n=20, single-dose crossover, erectile function endpoint) was located; no systematic review or long-term controlled safety study of chronic self-administered Melanotan II was found.
